source_excerpts.text:
## Mechanistic result A: Empty carrier is insufficient as a completion certificate
For upstream 3'-O-acylated DNA donor U–O–CO–P_n, both (1) productive aminoacyl transfer to an aminated downstream adaptor D and (2) hydrolysis to free chain P_n–COOH produce U–OH. A downstream Bst polymerase sensing only U–OH cannot distinguish the two. This is a formally exact observation under the listed reaction states; it does not assert the authors' physical apparatus has large hydrolysis. A similar false completion exists at PKS ACP–SH after productive translocation or failed hydrolysis. Product-qualified next-address state is needed, or acceptable hydrolysis leakage must be experimentally bounded. Chemical code alone cannot manufacture absent observation.

## Mechanistic result B: Ribosomal product custody preserves address for amide/ester step, not exotic motif completion
Let P carry chain P_n and A carry chosen monomer M_j encoded by the codon of the attached transcript T_j.
P_n–O–tRNA_P + H2N–M_j–O–tRNA_A -> tRNA_P–OH + P_n–C(O)–NH–M_j–O–tRNA_A.
Donor hydrolysis -> tRNA_P–OH + free P_n–COOH; leaves the incoming tRNA_A unchanged. Thus checking presence of the intact elongated product on A distinguishes these two chemical outcomes. The ribosome's ordinary elongation cycle structurally supports product custody and GTP-driven translocation, not an independent sensor that guarantees perfect product chemical identity. The same general mechanism can polymerize hydroxy acids via O-nucleophile to form ester links, if matched tRNA chemistry is used (Katoh 2026).
For Lee et al cyclic motifs, a second intramolecular hydrazine-to-ester condensation is REQUIRED after first peptidyl transfer. Thus even correct P->A transfer is NOT a certificate that the ring closed. The published same-system 22% ring / 78% linear example proves this limitation experimentally.

## Key current primary sources
- K. Lee et al., "Expanded ribosomal synthesis of non-standard cyclic backbones in vitro", *Nat. Commun.* (2025), DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-60126-4, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12120014/. Flexizyme-charged diester initiator and hydrazinoester tRNA, cell-free codon-decoded 5-/6-membered cyclic backbone; tested one 6-membered substrate yields approximately 22% cyclic and 78% linear; products linear react with 4-methylbenzaldehyde to yield hydrazone, which directly established availability of free N on unclosed state. In that particular test peptide was dried and dissolved in aldehyde prior to MALDI—not compatible with intact RNA code as performed. Some tested monomers yielded near 100% motif cyclization, but not uniform across substrates or positions. Two motif chemistry demonstrated, not a new idea here.
- Takayuki Katoh, "EF-P inhibits ribosomal alpha-hydroxy acid incorporation...", *RNA* (2026), DOI 10.1261/rna.081083.126, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13492118/. In cell-free translation, EF-P inhibits alpha-hydroxy on tRNAPro1E2 yet promotes beta/D amino acids. Assigning alpha-hydroxy to EF-P-insensitive AsnE2 and beta/D amino to EF-P-sensitive Pro1E2 allows same-bath multi-chemistry. Phe misincorporation side product observed; full code fidelity NOT established.
- R. Roberts and J. Szostak (1997), *PNAS*, DOI 10.1073/pnas.94.23.12297, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC24913/. mRNA–puromycin linked at 3' enters A site, receives nascent peptide and forms a stable covalent mRNA–product fusion; genotype/product pairing in a shared library is established.
- J. Johansen-Leete et al. (2026), *JACS*, DOI 10.1021/jacs.5c22682, https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41779940/. Genetically reprogrammed cyclic glycopeptides were produced and affinity-selected via mRNA display, including bioactive functional molecules; powerful incumbent.
- J. Bath & A. Turberfield, "Mechanism for a molecular assembler ... parallel DNA and a DNA polymerase", *Nanoscale Horizons* (2026), DOI 10.1039/D5NH00505A, https://pubs.rsc.org/en/content/articlehtml/2026/nh/d5nh00505a. Adaptor's 3'-OH released upon putative chain transfer primes Bst strand-displacing DNA polymerase to advance instructions. Primary article explicitly says all subcomponents investigated except the aminoacyl transfer steps: full assembly NOT demonstrated.
- R. Abdul

statement: For upstream 3'-O-acylated DNA donor U-O-CO-P_n, the listed productive transfer to a downstream aminated adaptor and hydrolysis of the acyl linkage both leave the upstream carrier in state U-OH. A downstream polymerase that senses only U-OH cannot distinguish the two outcomes. Thus donor-empty is not, by itself, a completion certificate. The failure is observational: an adequate next-address rule must also read a product-qualified receiving state, or the hydrolysis leakage must be separately bounded for the intended use.
title: An empty-carrier signal aliases productive transfer and hydrolysis in the stated assembly states
